key_cases.case_name: In the Interest of J. C. W.
key_cases.holding: The Court of Appeals vacated and remanded a juvenile court order awarding long-term custody of twins to their maternal aunt and uncle until their eighteenth birthday, holding that OCGA 15-11-58(i)(1) contains no statutory preference in favor of relative placement and that the juvenile court's contrary legal conclusion may have tainted its exercise of discretion.
key_cases.relevance: It is the closest Georgia appellate authority on the eighteenth-birthday terminus of a child-welfare custody disposition, holding that a long-term custody order runs to age 18 and that the children themselves are real parties in interest who may appeal it.
key_cases.quote: Because OCGA § 15-11-58 (i) (1) contains no preference in favor of relative placement, the juvenile court erred by finding otherwise.
